description: Make mo agent launch expose both the AgentJob result and the AgentSession conversation: add an AgentJob read surface, return both identities at launch, and unify the session conversation under a source-independent top-level mo session.

tasks.title: AgentJob relational read model and write-through grain persistence
tasks.description: Give AgentJob a queryable relational read model mirroring the AgentSession pattern, so jobs can be listed by agent and viewed by id. Add AgentJobRow (Infrastructure/Data/AgentJobs/AgentJobRow.cs) as a JSON State blob plus indexed columns (JobKey PK, ProjectId, AgentId, Status, SubmittedAt, TerminalAt), mirroring AgentSessionRow (Infrastructure/Data/Sessions/AgentSessionRow.cs). Register DbSet<AgentJobRow> on MohistDbContext (MohistDbContext.cs:37-74) with an OnModelCreating mapping using json_extract stored computed columns and a composite index on (AgentId, ProjectId, SubmittedAt), mirroring the AgentSessions mapping (MohistDbContext.cs:137-206), and add the EF migration. Add IAgentJobStore/AgentJobStore (LoadAsync(key) + SaveAsync(key, state) upsert) mirroring AgentSessionStore (Infrastructure/Data/Sessions/AgentSessionStore.cs), and AgentJobQuerier (Agent/Services/AgentJobQuerier.cs) with ListByAgentAsync(projectId, agentId, statusSet, limit) and GetByKeyAsync(jobKey), mirroring AgentSessionQuerier.ListAgentSessionsAsync. Migrate AgentJobGrain (Agent/Grains/AgentJobGrain.cs) to relational-authoritative persistence: inject IAgentJobStore, drop [PersistentState("agent-job")] (AgentJobGrain.cs:57), load state from the store on activation, and write the row on each persisted transition through the existing SaveAsync funnel (AgentJobGrain.cs:1151) — exactly as AgentSessionGrain does (AgentSessionGrain.cs:114). The grain string key (D1: agent-job-launch-{guid} / StableJobKey / CommentJobKey) is the row primary key. Register services in MohistServiceRegistration.cs (~line 105). This task delivers the storage/queryability that list-by-agent depends on; no HTTP or CLI surface yet (T-002 adds those). The read model is populated going forward as the grain transitions; jobs that pre-date cutover have no row until they next transition, so T-002's view route adds a grain fallback for those.
acceptanceCriteria: AgentJobState persists to a new AgentJobs relational table; the grain string key is the row primary key.

AgentJobGrain no longer uses [PersistentState]; it loads from IAgentJobStore on activation and writes the row synchronously on submit, runner-acceptance, and terminal transitions (one write per transition, no dual-write).
AgentJobQuerier.ListByAgentAsync returns jobs for (projectId, agentId) ordered most-recent-first with an optional status filter and limit; GetByKeyAsync returns the job for a key or null.
The full AgentJob lifecycle is unchanged: submit → running → completed|failed, dispatch retry/backoff, reminder-based recovery, terminal result reporting via ReportResultAsync still behave as before.
The AgentJobTerminalResult is reachable from the persisted row (status, message, output, artifactUploadIds, failureReason, exitCode).

server unit tests cover: AgentJobStore load/upsert, AgentJobQuerier list-by-agent (recency, status filter, empty) and view-by-key (hit/miss), and grain load-on-activate + write-on-transition — using injected fakes and no real DB or wall-clock.
Existing AgentJob spec tests (recovery, terminal transition, runner report, dispatch retry) still pass after the persistence migration.
npm run build (dotnet build) succeeds and npm test passes for the server.
tasks.output: AgentJobRow + DbSet + migration + AgentJobStore + AgentJobQuerier + DI registration; AgentJobGrain migrated to relational-authoritative write-through persistence.
tasks.notes: Design D1 (grain key = product job id / row PK) and D2 (read model mirroring AgentSession). The grain persistence migration is the top risk; mirror AgentSessionGrain's load-on-activate + write-on-transition exactly. If review finds the migration too risky, the documented fallback is a best-effort mirror write alongside [PersistentState] (D2 alternative a), accepted only with a follow-up to harden terminal-write consistency.

tasks.title: AgentJob read API surface and mo agent job CLI
tasks.spec: specs/agent-job-read/spec.md#View a single AgentJob by id
tasks.description: Expose the AgentJob status and terminal result over HTTP and the CLI. Add GET /api/projects/{projectRef}/agents/{agentRef}/jobs (list, mirroring AgentSessionListRoutes.cs) and GET /api/projects/{projectRef}/agent-jobs/{jobId} (view) reading AgentJobQuerier; register both in MohistApiRegistration.cs (~line 39). Add AgentJobListItemDto (jobId, agentId, agentName, status, submittedAt, terminalAt) and AgentJobViewDto carrying the AgentJobTerminalResult fields (status, message, output, artifactUploadIds, failureReason, exitCode); fields with no value are absent (null), never fabricated. Add the CLI agent job subgroup via BuildJob under agent (MohistCliCommands.Agent.cs:18): list <agent> → the list route, and view <job-id> → the view route, resolving the agent ref client-side like the existing session list. Add AgentJobList and AgentJobView to the TableShape enum (MohistCliApi.cs:1068), the cardinality switch, and the fields arms (ResourceOutput.cs:23-97). Return 404 for an unknown agent and an unknown job id; show current status for pending/running jobs without asserting a terminal result. The view route enforces project isolation: a job whose ProjectId differs from the route's projectRef returns 404. To keep every job addressable despite the read model being populated going forward, when a job id has no read-model row the view route falls back to reading the grain (GetStatusAsync + GetTerminalResultAsync, IAgentJobGrain.cs:10,18); list returns only projected jobs.
acceptanceCriteria: GET .../agents/{agentRef}/jobs returns the agent's jobs (id + status) most-recent-first; an agent with no jobs returns an empty list; an unknown agent returns 404.
GET .../agent-jobs/{jobId} returns the job's current status and, when terminal, its terminal result; an unknown job id returns 404.
GET .../agent-jobs/{jobId} returns 404 when the job's ProjectId does not match the route's projectRef (manual-launch keys are global GUIDs, so project isolation is enforced at the handler).

When a job id has no read-model row (a job that predates cutover and has not transitioned since), the view route falls back to the grain (GetStatusAsync + GetTerminalResultAsync) and still returns the job's status/result; list returns only jobs with rows.
A pending/running job view shows the current status and does not assert a terminal result.
The terminal result exposes status, message, output, artifactUploadIds, failureReason, and exitCode; absent values are null, not fabricated.
mo agent job list <agent> prints each job's id and status; mo agent job view <job-id> prints status and terminal result fields.

server spec tests cover: list-by-agent (jobs, empty, unknown-agent 404), view (completed, failed with failure reason, non-terminal, unknown-id 404, cross-project 404, grain-fallback when row absent), and terminal-result field completeness — via injected fakes, no real process/DB.
CLI spec tests cover: agent job list table output, agent job view output, unknown-agent and unknown-job error paths.
npm run build succeeds and npm test passes for server and cli.
tasks.output: AgentJob list/view HTTP routes + DTOs + DI/route registration; mo agent job list/view CLI commands and table shapes.
tasks.notes: Design D1 (job id = grain key, accepted by view) and the read-surface half of D2. The job id used by view is exactly the grain key / row PK. The view route enforces project isolation and falls back to the grain when no read-model row exists (covers jobs that pre-date cutover — see design 'Historical / in-flight jobs at cutover'). This is the canonical CLI read path for a job's terminal outcome (spec: AgentJob is the canonical work-result read path); the legacy result fields still carried on the Session DTO are removed by the separate #484, not here.

tasks.title: Launch returns both identities and mo agent launch CLI
tasks.spec: specs/agent-launch/spec.md#Launch returns both the AgentJob and AgentSession identities
tasks.description: Surface the AgentJob identity the launcher already mints, and relocate the launch command. Add JobKey to AgentLaunchResult (IAgentLauncher.cs:121); LaunchAsync (AgentLauncher.cs:111) and LaunchMentionAsync (AgentLauncher.cs:292) return the key they already compute (AgentLauncher.cs:124 and :256); the routed path already returns it (RoutedAgentLaunchOutcome.JobKey). Add JobId (and a job-result link) to AgentSessionLaunchResponse (AgentSessionLaunchRoutes.cs:203) and compose it from AgentLaunchResult.JobKey in the 201 handler (AgentSessionLaunchRoutes.cs:117). Relocate the CLI launch command: register BuildSessionLaunch directly under agent (MohistCliCommands.Agent.cs:18) instead of under the session subgroup, rename the user path to mo agent launch <agent>, and print both the job id and the session id; add jobId to the AgentSessionLaunch table shape (ResourceOutput.cs:68). Preserve the existing domain gates verbatim (whitespace prompt → 400 before any entity; unknown agent → 404; archived agent → 409; invalid context ref → error). No launch pipeline behaviour changes — only the returned identity and the command location. Close the launch gap note in docs/cli-reference.md:352.
acceptanceCriteria: AgentLaunchResult carries a non-empty JobKey for manual and mention launches; the routed path continues to return its key.
The launch 201 response includes a non-empty jobId alongside sessionId, agentId, agentName, and a transcript URL.
The jobId returned at launch is accepted verbatim by the T-002 view route (no id translation).
A launch still creates exactly one AgentJob and exactly one AgentSession and issues exactly one dispatch; submit/open ordering is unchanged.
mo agent launch <agent> prints both a job id and a session id; the command lives directly under agent (no intermediate session subcommand).
Domain gates are preserved: whitespace prompt → 400 with no session/job created; unknown agent → 404; archived agent → 409.
server spec tests cover: launch response carries jobId + sessionId, launched jobId is queryable via the job view route, exactly-one-job-and-one-session, and the three domain gates.
CLI spec tests cover: mo agent launch prints both ids; the relocated command path resolves the agent and posts to the launch route.
docs/cli-reference.md:352 gap note is closed; design/cli.md:67 (agent launch returns Job + Session) is aligned.
npm run build succeeds and npm test passes for server and cli.
tasks.output: AgentLaunchResult.JobKey; launch 201 carries jobId; mo agent launch CLI printing both ids; AgentSessionLaunch table shape includes jobId; launch gap note closed.
tasks.notes: Design D3 plus the launch half of D5. Depends on T-002 so the 'launched jobId is accepted by the read surface' acceptance is verifiable. Relocating launch out of the agent session subgroup is a prerequisite for T-005 removing that subgroup.

tasks.title: Source-agnostic unified session read route
tasks.spec: specs/session-command-unification/spec.md#Top-level session command addressed by stable Session ID
tasks.description: Add a project-scoped route group /api/projects/{projectRef}/sessions with GET /{sessionId} and GET /{sessionId}/transcript that resolve an AgentSession by id WITHOUT the source-kind == 'agent-launch' gate (contrast FindGenericSessionAsync, AgentSessionQuerier.cs:601-611, which 404s workflow sessions). The handlers read the session row by id and return a unified summary/transcript DTO carrying the fields common to both sources (id, source, activity, created/last-activity, model, usage, context refs), branching internally on the resolved source-kind to populate source-specific identity (agentId/agentName for agent-launch; workflowRunId/sessionName for workflow) via the absent-when-empty idiom. Add a unified list GET /api/projects/{projectRef}/sessions accepting ?agent=, ?issue=, ?run= filters that delegate to the existing querier methods (ListAgentSessionsAsync, ListSummariesByIssueAsync, ListByWorkflowAsync). Follow-up/cancel already accept an id for both sources and are not changed here. The older agent-sessions/{id} GET remains for the agent-launch transcript link until T-005 switches the CLI over.
acceptanceCriteria: GET .../sessions/{sessionId} returns the summary for an agent-launch session AND a workflow-originated session by the same stable id (no source-kind gate).
GET .../sessions/{sessionId}/transcript returns the transcript for both sources by id.
GET .../sessions with ?agent=, ?issue=, or ?run= returns sessions from the matching source; the filters delegate to the existing querier methods.
The unified summary DTO carries common fields and populates source-specific identity only for its source (workflow-only fields absent for agent-launch and vice-versa).
An unknown session id returns 404; a session belonging to a different project returns 404.
server spec tests cover: show/transcript by id for both sources, list by each filter, unknown-id 404, cross-project 404, and the source-specific-field contract — via injected fakes, no real DB.
npm run build succeeds and npm test passes for the server.
tasks.output: Unified project-scoped /sessions route group (show, transcript, source-filtered list) + unified DTO; no source-kind gate on id-keyed reads.
tasks.notes: Design D4. Independent of the AgentJob work (T-001..T-003), so it can run in parallel. The existing follow-up/cancel routes already resolve canonically by id for both sources, so only the read (show/transcript/list) routes need unifying. Resolves the --run project-scoping open question by making the unified list project-scoped (resolves project from the route, not from the run).

tasks.title: Top-level mo session CLI and retirement of duplicate session groups
tasks.spec: specs/session-command-unification/spec.md#Top-level session command addressed by stable Session ID
tasks.description: Add the top-level mo session command group and retire the duplicate source-specific groups. Add SessionCommands.Build(api) to the root command list (MohistCliCommands.Build): list (--agent/--issue/--run filters), show, transcript, followup, compact, reset, cancel — each taking a Session ID argument. show and transcript hit the T-004 unified /sessions routes; list hits the unified source-filtered route; followup/compact/reset/cancel hit the existing id-keyed action routes (which already accept an id for both sources). Remove the agent session subgroup (MohistCliCommands.Agent.cs:553, minus launch which T-003 already relocated) and the issue session / issue sessions groups (MohistCliCommands.Issue.Session.cs); mo issue sessions <num> is replaced by mo session list --issue <num>. mo session cancel requests runtime interruption only and must not cancel or rewrite the owning AgentJob lifecycle (the job remains the sole terminal authority). Close the session-unification gap note in docs/cli-reference.md:346 and align docs/agents.md (AgentJob/AgentSession ownership table).
acceptanceCriteria: mo session is a top-level command group; show/transcript/followup/compact/reset/cancel each take a Session ID and work for both agent-launch- and workflow-originated sessions.
mo session list accepts --agent, --issue, and --run; mo session list --issue <num> replaces mo issue sessions <num>.
mo session followup delivers a follow-up without creating a TaskRun or AgentJob.
mo session cancel requests runtime interruption only and does not transition the owning AgentJob to a terminal state.
The mo agent session and mo issue session(/sessions) command groups are removed; running them is command-not-found.
There is exactly one session command set; source is only a list filter, not a parallel capability.

CLI spec tests cover: session show/transcript by id for both sources, list by each filter, followup-no-job, cancel-runtime-only, and command-not-found for the retired agent session / issue session paths.
docs/cli-reference.md:346 gap note is closed; docs/agents.md ownership table is aligned.
npm run build succeeds and npm test passes for cli (CliAgentSessionCommandSpecs, CliIssueSessionSpecs updated).
tasks.output: Top-level mo session command group (list/show/transcript/followup/compact/reset/cancel by Session ID); agent session and issue session groups removed; session-unification gap note closed.
tasks.notes: Design D5 (session half) and D6. Depends on T-003 (launch already relocated out of the agent session subgroup before that subgroup is removed) and T-004 (unified read route the CLI targets). No aliases are kept (active-dev convention). Session archive/delete is explicitly out of scope (deferred to a follow-up).
